Rationale: Official memory docs cover short-term memory and memory concepts including semantic/episodic/procedural categories; stateful working memory is primarily LangGraph-backed.
Persistence/checkpoint/state support is strong; semantic/procedural memory can be implemented through stores but is less directly documented than graph state.
Official memory docs expose short-term, long-term/entity/contextual memory and agent-level memory behavior; explicit truncation is less central.
Agent memory and semantic indexing support are documented; procedural/preference memory is not a first-class dimension in the official agent memory docs.
Buffered/token-limited model context and memory protocol support recent context and state; long-term semantic/procedural support is more limited.
Haystack has message objects, agents, and strong document-store/retrieval support, but agent memory as a full taxonomy is limited.
ChatHistory and reducers support recent context/truncation/summarization; vector store and plugins support semantic/procedural roles, but episodic memory is less explicit.
Memory module and vector-backed memory support several memory roles; procedural/preference memory is less directly documented.
Role memory and role/action context support history/state/procedure-like behavior, but context truncation and semantic memory are less uniformly documented.
Classic profile/memory mechanisms exist, but stable official API evidence is incomplete and memory support is narrower.
